Title: Diagnosis
Details: The failure is caused by an overflow exception thrown when constructing a BigFraction from a double (0.5000000001) with a maxDenominator of 10. The relevant constructor `BigFraction(double value, int maxDenominator)` delegates to a private constructor with signature `BigFraction(double value, double epsilon, int maxDenominator, int maxIterations)` which includes the main fraction approximation algorithm.

This constructor uses a continued fraction approach and keeps track of numerators (p) and denominators (q) at each iteration. The variables p2 and q2 represent the numerator and denominator of the current convergent being evaluated. The overflow limit is set to Integer.MAX_VALUE.

During each iteration, if either p2 or q2 exceeds this overflow limit, it throws a FractionConversionException. According to the code, this can happen after calculating a new convergent if p2 or q2 is too large. The comment around the overflow check suggests that in maxDenominator mode, if the last fraction was very close to the value, q2 might overflow in the next iteration, and in that case, they choose to throw an exception.

In the test case, the input double 0.5000000001 is very close to the simple fraction 1/2. Because the fraction approximation involves iterated denominators and numerators that grow, the code likely overflows the integer limit with either p2 or q2 before terminating properly, hence throwing the exception instead of returning the fraction closest to the input with denominator less than or equal to 10. The test expects that this situation should not throw an exception if the value is sufficiently close to a simple fraction within the given maxDenominator constraint.

Thus, the root cause is the incomplete handling of the case where the fraction is very close to a simple fraction, but the iteration causes p2 or q2 to overflow before the stopping conditions recognize the proximity. This leads to an inappropriate overflow exception instead of returning a suitable fraction approximation.

Recent bug reports are unrelated or about other classes, so do not provide additional insights here. The issue is localized in the fraction approximation loop of `BigFraction(double, double, int, int)` constructor with the overflow check and stopping conditions.

Next step would be to fix this constructor to better handle this edge case near simple fractions to avoid premature overflow exceptions by potentially returning the previous fraction in such cases or improving the overflow detection logic.
